Well, the luck and skill that it took to make this happen – I am boggled.  Making these loops work horizontally and vertically, what crazy work of trial and error, and grid design, and there are six of these things!

What???  So okay, crossnerd me is blown away.  This is WEI WEI impressive.

I never feel like Adam’s puzzles are just showing off, though.  I always feel that twinkle in his eye – he’s an entertainer, and his puzzles bring smiles to my heart.  (Just look at [Deals made on the spot?] for AD SALES.) 

And OMG can he stick with a challenge.

There were some sticky fill-in points to make my brain happy, but there were plenty of easier areas to fill in, and I’m grateful for them, so I could sit back and just admire the beauty and virtuosity pulsing in the box.  It turned out to be a very sweet solve.

This, then, is a how-did-you-do-it and I’m-so-glad-you-did-it, Adam.  Thank you!

O Brave New World!
I say that because coincidentally I just finished Jeff Chen’s puzzle from 2016 that Adam referenced with a similar theme, and it led me to ponder how far we have come in 10 years. I was absolutely amazed by the skill and craft in Jeff’s puzzle, but this one blew that one away technically. Sure it was done with a lot of computer help (but not AI, based in Adam’s description, in case you were wondering)—but that’s not a bad thing. And as Adam stated it still took a lot of help from the crossword gods to make this work.

And the rest of this puzzle was equally precise in its technique and fill. And a decent challenge for a Sunday. Sometime I find a bit of a lack of fun factor in these technical creations—but these were pretty fun themers, not to mention the fun factor of solving them, marveling at their creation, some fun entries like SMOREO and EARGASM and fun clues like those for AGEISM and ORATORY.

So it’s clear that in some ways tech savvy constructors like Adam are starting to leave the rest of us in the dust. And I say, good for them. I think there will always still be a place for old school constructing—there was a charm to Jeff’s puzzle that just can’t be reproduced. And in some ways the newer crossword nerds may end up feeling like modern cruise captains, wistfully imagining early explorers sailing into unknown waters with only their sextants and rusty chronometers. But that doesn’t mean I want to take a cruise on them.

Unsolicited tip for newer solvers: on Sundays (along with ever other day, but especially Sunday), don’t spend much time puzzling over any one spot until you have made your way through the entire grid.

Weird little gray squares that are clearly part of some kinda funky structural theme? Noted, but ignoring until I get to a point where I *need* the theme mechanics to fill something in.

Some actor’s name from Stranger Things that I certainly don’t know? Won’t even give that the slightest bit of thought unless I end up needing to infer one letter (which I didn’t in this case, as SADIE came entirely from crosses).

Clues that are obviously meant to be ambiguous? I *might* plunk down a quick guess if one comes to mind, but it’s often better to wait for at least a letter or two from crosses, which will rule out most possibilities.
